sentences.text:
Arbinder Dang vs Manmeet Kaur on 27 September, 2024
 Cnr No. Dlwt010031902024
 Cr. Rev. 1922024
 Ps Kirti Nagar
 Arbinder Dang v. State and Anr.

. 
Present: Revisionist in person with Ld. Counsel, Sh. Vishal
 Kumar.

Dr. Darvesh Yadav, Ld. Additional Pp for the
 State/Respondent no.1.
1.

Matter is listed today for orders.
2.
Arguments have already been heard on behalf of the Revisionist and State.
None has come forward on behalf of Respondent n.2/complainant to argue the present revision petition despite due service.
No written arguments or reply has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2 despite opportunity.
3. TCR has been received and is carefully perused.

4. By way of present revision petition, revisionist Arbinder Dang who was kept in column no. 12 while filing chargesheet in case FIR No. 191/2019 PS Kirti Nagar has challenged the impugned order dated 12.03.2024 whereby she was summoned to be tried as an accused.
5. Brief facts of the case are that the present FIR was registered u/s 498A/406/34 IPC on the basis of a complaint made by Smt. Manmeet Kaur.
After investigation, chargesheet was filed against accused Gurbinder Singh, husband of the complainant u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.

Revisionist Dr.
Arbinder Dang, nanad of the complainant was kept in column no. 12 by the IO and not chargesheeted as sufficient evidence was not gathered against her.
Chargesheet was filed on 22.01.2021.

Ld. Trial Court took cognizance Contd..2..
2 vide order dated 24.06.2022 and directed summoning of accused whose name was mentioned in column no.11 i.e. accused Gurbinder Singh.
No directions were passed regarding summoning of accused kept in column no. 12 i.e. Revisionist Dr. Arbinder Dang.
Accused Gurbinder Singh appeared before the court on 31.10.2022 and was admitted to bail.

After supplying the copy of the chargesheet to accused Gurbinder Singh, matter was listed for scrutiny of documents/consideration on charge on 12.03.2024.
6.

Vide order dated 12.03.2024, on the submissions of Ld. Additional PP for the State as well as Ld.
Counsel for the complainant regarding specific allegations against the revisionist Dr. Arbinder Dang whose name was mentioned in column no. 12 and after going through the record directed summoning of revisionist Dr. Arbinder Dang for facing trial u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.
It is this order which is under challenge in the present revision petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted on behalf of the revisionist that the impugned order is bad in law as it amounts to review of its own order by Ld. Trial Court as vide order dated 24.06.2022, it was specifically directed that only accused kept in column no.11 was to be summoned.
Consequently, Ld. Trial Court vide order dated 24.06.2022 had consciously decided not to summon the revisionist Dr. Arbinder Dang who was kept in column no.12.
After two years of passing of the said order, Ld. Trial Court, again on the basis of same material directed summoning of the revisionist which amounts to review of its earlier order.
Accordingly, setting aside of the impugned order is prayed.

8. Per contra, it is submitted on behalf of the State that Contd...3..
3

there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned order dated 12.03.2024 as the summoning of revisionist Dr. Arbinder Dang has been made on the basis of allegations contained against her in the complaint on the basis of which present FIR has been registered.
Accordingly, dismissal of the present revision petition is sought.
9. I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record.
10. It is a settled law that at the stage of taking cognizance of offence, provisions of Section 190 CrPC would be applicable.
Section 190 inter alia provides that, "The Magistrate may take cognizance of any offence upon a police report of such facts which constitute an offence".
Accordingly, as per this provision, the Magistrate takes cognizance of an offence and not the offender.
After taking cognizance of the offence, the Magistrate u/s 204 CrPC is empowered to issue process to the accused.
At the stage of issuing process, it is for the Magistrate to decide whether process should be issued against particular person/persons named in the chargesheet and also not named therein.
For that purpose, he is required to consider the FIR and the statements recorded by the police officer and other documents tendered along with the chargesheet.

Further, upon receipt of police report u/s 173 (2) CrPC, the Magistrate is entitled to take cognizance of an offence u/s 190(1)(b) even if the police report is to the effect that no case is made out against the accused by ignoring the conclusion arrived at by the investigating officer and independently applying his mind to the facts emerging from the investigation by taking into account the statement of the witnesses examined by the police.

At this Contd...4..
4 stage, there is no question of application of Section 319 CrPC (Reliance in this regard is placed upon decision of the Apex Court in M/s Swil Ltd.Vs State Crl Appeal no. 820/2001 order dated 14.08.2001).
11.

entities.text: M/s Swil Ltd.Vs State Crl Appeal no. 820/2001
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has also been held by the Apex court in Raghubans Dubey Vs State of Bihar (1967) 2 SCR 423 that, " In our opinion, once cognizance is taken by the Magistrate, he takes cognizance of an offence and not the offenders; once he takes cognizance of the offence, it is his duty to find out who the offenders really are and once he comes to the conclusion that apart from the persons sent up by the police, some other persons are involved, it is his duty to proceed against those persons.

entities.text: Raghubans Dubey Vs State of Bihar (1967) 2 SCR 423
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The summoning of the additional accused is a part of the proceedings initiated by his taking cognizance of an offence".

Arbinder Dang vs Manmeet Kaur on 27 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90548320/
2 12.

entities.text: Arbinder Dang vs Manmeet Kaur on 27 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is trite that after taking cognizance of the offence, the Magistrate can summon any person as an accused to be tried for that offence, if he is of the opinion that considering the investigation done in the matter and the evidence collected by the IO, the said person appears to be an offender whether or not he is chargesheeted as an accused by the IO.

The second stage of summoning an additional accused arises u/s 319 CrPC when on the basis of additional evidence that comes on record, some other person not being tried appears to be one of the offender who needs to be tried along with the accused persons already facing trial.
This law has been repeatedly reiterated by Superior Courts in various judgments.
13. Now, coming to the facts of the present case, perusal of order dated 24.06.2022 whereby Ld.

Trial Court took cognizance of the Contd...5..
5 offences and directed issuance of summons to accused shows that there were specific directions for summoning of accused mentioned in column no. 11 only thereby declining to summon the revisionist/accused mentioned in column no.12.
Matter is still at the stage of consideration of charge and no new evidence has come on record till date.

When, once Ld. Trial Court had once refused to summon accused mentioned at column no. 12, then on the basis of same material directing summoning of accused mentioned in column no. 12 at this stage would amount to review of its own order by Ld. Trial Court which is not permitted by law.

Accordingly, I deem it appropriate to set aside the impugned order dated 12.03.2024 directing summoning of revisionist/accused Dr.
Arbinder Dang at this stage.
Needless to say, accused Dr. Arbinder Dang may be summoned u/s 319 CrPC if any additional evidence comes on record against her at a later stage.
14. With these directions, the present revision petition is allowed and impugned order dated 12.03.2024 directing summoning of Revisionist herein as an accused is set aside.
15. Revisionist is directed to furnish bail bond in the sum of Rs. 15000/ with one surety in the like amount u/s 437A CrPC within one week from today.
16. TCR be sent back along with copy of this order.
17. Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
